A manufacturing process gradually increases the size of a square opening by lengthening its diagonals at a rate of $1.6\text{ mm}\text{/s}.$ At what rate is the area of the opening increasing when each diagonal measures $25\,\text{mm}?$

The area is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
${\text{mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $h$ and $A$ be the length of the diagonals and the area of the square, respectively. Using the Pythagorean theorem, it can be shown that the relationship between $A$ and $h$ is

$$
A=\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}.
$$

We want to find

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}h}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot h.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $h$ increases at a rate of $1.6\,\text{mm/s},$ so

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=1.6.
$$

Also, we want to compute the rate of change of the area when the diagonal has length $h=25.$ Substituting this information into our expression for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =1.6\cdot 25=40{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the area of the square opening is increasing at a rate of 
$40{\text{ mm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$
